subject: Threshold latency surge — lane coordination & KV cache mitigation
messages:
From: Ashley Miller <ashley.miller@threshold.ai>
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@threshold.ai
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden P99 latency + 5xx increase on prod - help needed

Hi Logan,

We started seeing a sharp P99 latency spike and a growing 5xx rate on our production tenant around 08:45 PT. Throughput is steady but tail latency has doubled and a portion of requests started getting 502/503. This is customer-visible and blocking our release tonight.

We've attached sampling logs and a short trace. Ops observed a pattern where a small set of prefixes are getting hot and eviction churn is high. Any quick suggestions? Can you escalate to someone in infra/runtime please — we need an emergent mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Ashley
Director of Engineering, Threshold AI

Attachments: threshold-ops-logs-20290516.tar.gz

---
Note: forwarding full trace to your team.

From: logan.wright@redwood.ai
To: Ashley Miller <ashley.miller@threshold.ai>, ops@threshold.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden P99 latency + 5xx increase on prod - help needed

Ashley — thanks for the fast heads-up and the logs. I'm pulling in Ben (runtime ops) and Marissa (CS lead) to coordinate.

Quick read: logs show rapid KV eviction events and repeated prefix loads for ~12 keys accounting for ~48% of recent traffic. That aligns with a hotset thrash / head-of-line blocking scenario in our priority-lane scheduling.

Immediate plan (30/90/240 mins):
- 0-30m: Apply temporary per-tenant burst limit (throttle) for heavy prefixes to prevent HOL blocking.
- 30-90m: Switch Threshold tenant to conservative cache retention (reduce prefix TTL, raise eviction aggressiveness) and split top hot prefixes into a dedicated hot-lane to isolate batching lanes.
- 90-240m: Roll a safe runtime config that disables the recent kernel prefetch optimization (if correlated) and monitor.

Can Threshold ops stand by for a short call at 10:00 PT? We'll share a mitigation playbook and keep you updated.

—Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Ashley Miller <ashley.miller@threshold.ai>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden P99 latency + 5xx increase on prod - help needed

Looping in Jon for runtime kernel knobs. I dug into the attached samples:
- High observed KV eviction rate (evictions/sec spikes 6x baseline) with eviction-reinserts for the same prefixes.
- Batching lane logs show repeated stall where hot requests hold the lane for long synth sequences (HOL). Backpressure then starves other lanes, causing timeouts and some 502s when requests queue out.

Temporary actions taken (09:40 PT):
- Enabled tenant-level burst token bucket (rate cap 120 rps sustained, 400 rps burst).
- Pinned top-12 hot prefixes to a dedicated hot-lane with reduced max-batch-size to avoid long sync stalls.

Next steps (owner):
- Ben: monitor p99 + eviction rates over next 60m.
- Jon: prepare rollback for recent prefetch kernel change and a config that shortens prefix TTL.
- Logan / Marissa: coordinate comms and exec update if we need an SLA allowance.

I'll publish a concise playbook (lane-mitigation-playbook-v1.pdf) and the logs to the ops ticket.

—Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Ashley Miller <ashley.miller@threshold.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden P99 latency + 5xx increase on prod - help needed

Update after quick runtime probe:
- The kernel prefetch optimization introduced last week increases prefetch aggressiveness for longer tokens which is beneficial normally, but in this workload it amplifies hot-prefix re-loads and pushes eviction churn.
- Memory occupancy on the KV cache for the tenant jumped ~30% in the last 15 minutes prior to the spike.

Action plan executed (11:00 PT):
1) Disabled the prefetch optimization for Threshold tenant (feature flag).
2) Shortened prefix retention from 20m -> 6m for the tenant.
3) Applied a soft TTL jitter to reduce synchronized cache re-population.

Preliminary effects (11:15 PT): P99 trending down ~28%, eviction/sec down ~60% from peak, total 5xx beginning to taper. No regressions observed in throughput.

I'll keep the feature flag off for 24h and prepare a follow-up patch that scopes prefetch aggressiveness based on prefix churn metrics.

-Jonas
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: logan.wright@redwood.ai
To: Ashley Miller <ashley.miller@threshold.ai>, ops@threshold.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden P99 latency + 5xx increase on prod - help needed

Ashley — follow-up and summary for your execs:

What happened: A narrow hotset of prefixes triggered repeated prefetch + heavy reuse that caused eviction thrash in the shared KV cache and head-of-line blocking in the priority batching lanes. That led to lane starvation, queue overruns, and elevated 5xx.

What we did (summary):
- Immediate: tenant burst throttle + dedicate a hot-lane for top hot prefixes (reduced batch sizes).
- Short term (hours): disabled prefetch optimization for the tenant, shortened prefix TTL, added jittered TTL and increased eviction aggressiveness for the tenant.
- Medium term (days): implement automated hot-key detection to auto-isolate prefixes, per-tenant KV quotas, and adaptive prefetch that backs off on churn.

Current status: P99 and 5xx are back near baseline; eviction churn dropped significantly. We will keep the tenant on conservative settings for 24h and then run a controlled canary of an adaptive prefetch patch.

Action items for Threshold:
- Confirm if you want us to keep the conservative settings for 72h (recommended) or flip earlier.
- Share any release windows to avoid during the canary.

If you'd like, Marissa and I can prepare a short executive note for your leadership summarizing impact and remediation.

Thanks for being patient — we'll follow up with the full postmortem and a set of preventive controls.

—Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: lane-mitigation-playbook-v1.pdf
